newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repos end down on rate cut rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repos end down on rate cut rumours.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down in slow trading on Wednesday on rumours that the central bank would cut bank interest rates in the first quarter of this year, traders said.
Central bank officials have declined to comment.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 10.00 percent from 11.68 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover fell to 2.97 million lots from 6.61 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The rumours were a major factor today," said one trader.
Traders said a major policy meeting on banking and finance issues, to be held in Beijing next week, was another reason for the falls today.
"Many institutions stayed on the sidelines today, waiting for the outcome from the bank meeting," said a second trader.
Traders expect repo rates to remain weak in the short term before the outcome of the meeting is made public.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed with the most active 10-year contract falling on profit-taking after rises on Tuesday, traders said.
The 10-year bond that matures in 2006, a market barometer, fell to 118.02 yuan from 118.45 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.51 million lots from 1.87 million.
Traders said they believed the contracts would move in a narrow range before the Chinese Lunar New Year in early February with institutions busy settling year-end accounts.
But falling inflation and the expected lower coupon rates for new issues of state debt this year was likely to support the prices of the existing contracts in the mid-term, they said.
